answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a cross-verified trade mesh: every identity must hold a history of completed deals with counterparties who themselves hold verified meshes, like a lotus root system where each stem links to many others. A fake cluster forms a closed loop with no edges into the honest mesh, so its offers are quarantined automatically. To forge one edge an attacker must buy a real deal from an honest agent at market price, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand real deals — the umber ledger of that expense is crystal clear to anyone checking the graph.
